title: math-exercise – Overview of All Check Modes
text: This page briefly introduces and lets you try out every check mode of the math-exercise extension. See the README for full option details.

title: math-exercise – Overview of All Check Modes
text:
mode: equivalent (default)
Accepts any mathematically equivalent representation.

equivalent


Compute the area of a circle with r = 3 cm.
A =  cm²


  ✓ Check
  ⓘ Input help
  
    💬 Feedback
    ⚙
  






  Show source
  ```{math-exercise}
#| label: ex-equivalent
#| caption: equivalent
Compute the area of a circle with r = 3 cm.
A = _[pi * 9] cm²
```

Try pi*9, 9*pi, and 3**2*pi – all are accepted.

title: math-exercise – Overview of All Check Modes
text:
mode: exact
The strictest check mode: accepts only the canonical SymPy representation.

exact (numeric fraction)


Give 6/8 fully reduced: 


  ✓ Check
  ⓘ Input help
  
    💬 Feedback
    ⚙
  






  Show source
  ```{math-exercise}
#| label: ex-exact-numeric
#| caption: exact (numeric fraction)
#| mode: exact
Give 6/8 fully reduced: _[3/4]
```

3/4 is accepted. 6/8 is rejected – even though SymPy reduces 6/8 and 3/4 to the same internal object on parse, mode: exact additionally checks the raw text you typed for un-reduced numeric fractions (including ones hidden inside expressions like 1/4 + 2/4).

exact (algebraic)


Give the factored form of x² + 2x + 1: 


  ✓ Check
  ⓘ Input help
  
    💬 Feedback
    ⚙
  






  Show source
  ```{math-exercise}
#| label: ex-exact
#| caption: exact (algebraic)
#| vars: x
#| mode: exact
Give the factored form of x² + 2x + 1: __[(x+1)**2]
```

(x+1)**2 is accepted. x**2+2*x+1 is mathematically equivalent but a different representation, so it’s rejected as “correct, but not in the requested form”.

title: math-exercise – Overview of All Check Modes
text:
reject (add-on for equivalent)
Rejects one specific – mathematically equivalent – expression. Useful for simplification tasks.

equivalent + reject


Simplify (x+1)²: 


  ✓ Check

    💬 Feedback
    ⚙

  ```{math-exercise}
#| label: ex-reject
#| caption: equivalent + reject
#| vars: x
#| mode: equivalent
#| reject: (x+1)**2
Simplify (x+1)²: __[x**2 + 2*x + 1]
```

(x+1)^2 and (1+x)^2 are rejected; x^2 + 2x + 1 is accepted.

title: math-exercise – Overview of All Check Modes
section: mode: custom — monotone increasing with flat points allowed
text:
mode: custom — monotone increasing with flat points allowed
This checker receives the student’s parsed SymPy expression and verifies that its derivative is non-negative on \([0,1]\) and that the function rises overall.

custom SymPy checker


Give an example of a monotonically increasing function on $[0,1]$:

$f(x) =$ 


  ✓ Check
  ⓘ Input help
  
    💬 Feedback
    ⚙
  






  Show source
  ```{math-exercise}
#| label: ex-custom-monotonicity
#| caption: custom SymPy checker
#| vars: x
#| mode: custom
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       f = response["expressions"][0]
#|       x = symbols["x"]
#|       lower = minimum(diff(f, x), x, Interval(0, 1))
#|       rise = simplify(f.subs(x, 1) - f.subs(x, 0))
#|       if lower.is_nonnegative is True and rise.is_positive is True:
#|           return {
#|               "score": 1.0,
#|               "feedback": "The derivative is non-negative and the function rises overall."
#|           }
#|       return {
#|           "score": 0.0,
#|           "feedback": "Non-decreasing behavior with an overall rise was not established."
#|       }

Give an example of a monotonically increasing function on $[0,1]$:

$f(x) =$ ___[]
```

Try x, x**2 + x, and x**2. All three are accepted; isolated zero derivatives and flat portions are allowed, provided the function never decreases and rises overall.

JSXGraph response — editable freehand polynomial approximation
Draw a curve across \([0,1]\). JSXGraph simplifies the captured pointer samples to nine fixed-x adjustment points and fits a degree-five regression polynomial. After you move one blue point, all blue points are projected back onto the new red polynomial. Assessment uses dense samples of that polynomial.


Draw, adjust, and fit a monotonically increasing function

increasing, allowing flat portions. After drawing, adjust the blue points as needed.
Their x-coordinates stay fixed; when you release a point, every blue point is

title: math-exercise – Overview of All Check Modes
section: AI feedback with reusable mini-machine context
text:
AI feedback with reusable mini-machine context
This example is adapted and translated from the mini-machine exercises.


Mini-machine number representation
The mini-machine uses the simplified floating-point format
\[
\boxed{S}\quad\boxed{EEE}\quad\boxed{MMMM},
\]
where:

\(S\) is one sign bit;
\(E\) is a three-bit exponent field;
\(M\) is a four-bit mantissa field;
the exponent bias is \(3\).

Only normalized numbers with \(E=1,2,\ldots,6\) are used. The bit patterns \(E=0\) and \(E=7\) are excluded, so this mini-machine ignores subnormal numbers, infinities, and NaNs.
A bit pattern represents the number
\[
(-1)^S\left(1+\frac{M}{16}\right)2^{E-3},
\]
where \(M\) is the integer value of the four mantissa bits.
For example,
\[
0\;|\;100\;|\;0110
\]
has \(S=0\), \(E=(100)_2=4\), \(e=4-3=1\), and \(M=(0110)_2=6\). Therefore,
\[
x=(1+6/16)2^1=2.75.
\]
To encode a representable number, first write it as
\[
\pm(1.MMMM)_2\,2^e.
\]
Then determine the sign bit, calculate the stored exponent \(E=e+3\), and write \(S\), \(E\), and \(M\) as bit fields.



Problem 1A — decode a bit pattern
Calculate the value represented by the bit pattern.

Decode a mini floating-point number


↻



  ✓ Check
  ⓘ Input help
  
    💬 Feedback
    ⚙
  






  Show source
  ```{math-exercise}
#| label: ex-mini-decode
#| caption: Decode a mini floating-point number
#| pool: true
#| mode: equivalent
#| context: mini-machine-representation

$$0\;|\;100\;|\;0110$$

The represented value is: _[11/4]

---

$$0\;|\;101\;|\;0110$$

The represented value is: _[11/2]

---

$$1\;|\;100\;|\;0000$$

The represented value is: _[-2]

---

$$0\;|\;011\;|\;1000$$

The represented value is: _[3/2]

---

$$0\;|\;010\;|\;0100$$

The represented value is: _[5/8]
```



Problem 1B — encode a number
Fill in the sign, exponent, and mantissa fields.

Encode a number in the mini-machine format

title: AI feedback and learning context
text:
The Feedback button can request progressive hints from an OpenAI-compatible model. Credentials and model choice are stored only in the student’s browser. Ordinary answer checking does not require an AI service.
The extension sends the exact task, the student’s current work, private checker results, the current hint level, and the relevant learning context. It asks the model to preserve the document language and to return concise student-facing feedback without exposing internal reasoning.

title: AI feedback and learning context
text:
Provider compatibility
The model capability adapter uses a portable request body for unknown OpenAI-compatible providers. It adds low-reasoning controls only for recognised model families and retries once with the portable baseline if a provider rejects optional parameters. See the adapter design notes for the policy and known limitations.

title: Custom assessment with SymPy
text:
mode: custom runs trusted, instructor-authored SymPy/Python once for the complete response. This is useful when correctness means satisfying a property or a relationship rather than matching one predetermined expression.
The checker receives response["expressions"], an ordered list of parsed SymPy expressions, and symbols, a dictionary containing the names declared in vars. It may return a boolean, a score from 0 to 1, or a dictionary containing score or correct and optional plain-text feedback.

title: Custom assessment with SymPy

1. Assess a mathematical property
This accepts any function that is non-decreasing on \([0,1]\) and rises overall; there is no single canonical answer. Try x, x^2, or x^3+x.
